key_insight: A fully discrete finite element scheme for Kirchhoff-type equations achieves optimal spatial accuracy and second-order time accuracy, while preserving discrete energy for homogeneous problems with constant coefficients.
engineering_relevance: The method supports accurate simulation of nonlocal nonlinear structural dynamics where energy consistency helps control numerical artifacts.
method: Conforming finite elements of arbitrary polynomial degree p in two spatial dimensions.
Picard iteration for the nonlinearity, with convergence and error analysis.
evidence_signal: Manufactured-solution experiments reproduce second-order temporal convergence and spatial L² convergence of order h^(p+1), consistent with the theoretical error bounds.
watch_item: Exact discrete energy preservation is established only for the homogeneous, constant-coefficient problem; the general convergence results require the paper’s stated hypotheses.
paper_title: Conservative Finite Element Methods for Kirchhoff-Type Equations
